title: Beatrix and the Cover
premise: Theo Eriksen has spent twelve years as a fixer for the Meridian Office, an embassy that exists on no map, erasing people and secrets for a government that denies him. When a real estate listing surfaces showing the interior of his own safe house — down to the photograph of his dead sister on the shelf — Theo realizes someone inside the Office is selling them out, one property at a time. His hunt for the leak drags him through Vienna's underworld to Ilse Brandt, a former asset who holds the secret worth killing for: proof that the Office's director built his career on a massacre he blamed on Theo. As dawn and the extraction flight approach, Theo must choose between burning the evidence to save himself or delivering it to expose the director, knowing either choice makes him a target forever. He trades the secret to a journalist mid-tarmac, boards the flight as bait, and ends the book alive but officially erased — finally free because no one is looking for a man who doesn't exist.
about_author: Astrid Fairweather is a former diplomatic translator who spent a decade in European capital cities before turning to fiction. She writes thrillers about the invisible machinery of power from a farmhouse in rural Norway.

chapters.title: The Listing
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Scrolling property listings at 2 a.m., Theo finds his safe house photographed room by room, including personal effects that should have been incinerated. The emotional beat is cold dread: twelve years of discipline undone by a realtor's wide-angle lens.

chapters.title: House Rules
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Flashback woven into present: how Theo joined the Meridian Office after his sister's death, and the rules that govern fixers — never be photographed, never keep souvenirs, never trust the second floor. Beat: uneasy nostalgia curdling into suspicion.

chapters.title: The Second Floor
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. He reports the breach to Deputy Director Voss, who is oddly calm and orders Theo to stand down. Theo notices Voss's assistant, Katarin, watching him leave. Beat: first taste of institutional gaslighting.

chapters.title: Katarin
chapters.summary: Katarin's POV. She copies files from Voss's office, revealing the listing was posted from an internal terminal. She doesn't know yet if she's a whistleblower or a pawn. Beat: fear sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: Ilse
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Following the listing's digital trail to Prague, Theo finds Ilse Brandt, a retired asset living under a name the Office gave her. She recognizes him instantly and says, 'They're selling us all, piece by piece.' Beat: reluctant alliance.

chapters.title: What Ilse Kept
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. Ilse reveals she holds a sealed dossier proving Director Halvorsen orchestrated the Ljubljana convoy massacre and pinned it on a young fixer named Eriksen. Beat: Theo's world tilts — his loyalty was purchased with a lie.

chapters.title: Twelve Years of Silence
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo confronts his own complicity: jobs he executed without questions, names he erased. He realizes the listing wasn't a mistake; it was bait meant to flush out whoever still had the dossier. Beat: shame and fury braided together.

chapters.title: The Buyer
chapters.summary: Katarin's POV. Katarin traces the listing to a private broker working for Halvorsen's rival inside the ministry — someone else wants the dossier too. Beat: the conspiracy widens; no side is clean.

chapters.title: Safe House, Unsafe
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Returning to the safe house to retrieve contingency documents, Theo walks into a staged burglary team. He escapes through the crawlspace he installed himself, wounded. Beat: paranoia made physical.

chapters.title: Stitches and Lies
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. Ilse patches Theo's shoulder in her kitchen and tests his motives: does he want justice or absolution? Their argument turns intimate, two survivors recognizing each other. Beat: tenderness inside distrust.

chapters.title: Voss Calls
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Voss summons Theo home, offering promotion and protection if he surrenders 'any legacy materials.' It's a confession wrapped in an offer. Beat: the trap closing politely.

chapters.title: The Extraction Flight
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo learns his own extraction is scheduled for dawn — one way, no return manifest. The Office isn't relocating him; it's disappearing him. Beat: betrayal crystallized into logistics.

chapters.title: Katarin's Choice
chapters.summary: Katarin's POV. Caught copying files, Katarin bargains with Voss by offering Theo's location, buying herself a day. Guilt hits hard when she sees the flight manifest. Beat: survival at the price of someone else.

chapters.title: Night Train to Vienna
chapters.summary: Theo and Ilse's alternating POV. They move the dossier by rail, dodging Office surveillance through crowded carriages. A near-miss with a tail forces them to trust each other completely. Beat: partnership forged under pressure.

chapters.title: The Broker's Table
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo meets the broker who posted the listing and learns Halvorsen authorized it personally — a message to Ilse: I know you kept it. Beat: the hunt reframed as a duel between old enemies.

chapters.title: What Belonging Costs
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. Ilse admits she stayed silent for thirty years because the Office was the only place she belonged. Now she wants the truth public even if it kills her. Beat: theme stated — belonging can be a cage.

chapters.title: Halvorsen
chapters.summary: Halvorsen's POV. The director dines with ministers, charming and untouchable, while ordering Theo's termination framed as defection. We see power as performance. Beat: chilling elegance of corruption.

chapters.title: The Trade
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo negotiates with journalist Mara Lindqvist: the full dossier in exchange for publication within hours, not weeks. Mara warns him there's no undoing this. Beat: point of no return chosen deliberately.

chapters.title: Airport Lights
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. At the airfield, Katarin defects and hands Theo the terminal logs implicating Voss. Office teams converge on the tarmac. Beat: chaos erupting as dawn breaks.

chapters.title: Dawn
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Climax: Theo trades the dossier's decryption key to Mara on the tarmac as extraction agents close in; Ilse creates a diversion that costs her freedom. Theo boards the flight as the story goes live worldwide. Beat: sacrifice and release.

chapters.title: Erased
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Mid-flight, Theo watches news alerts detonate across Europe. Halvorsen resigns within hours; the Office begins quietly dismantling itself. Theo has no passport, no name, no handler. Beat: terrifying liberty.

chapters.title: A Man Who Doesn't Exist
chapters.summary: Theo's POV, epilogue. Months later, Theo lives under a new name in a coastal town, visited once by Katarin. He keeps no photographs now — except one, of Ilse, taken openly in daylight. Beat: belonging chosen, not assigned; survival paid in full.
